movie.title: Slanted
movie.overview: An insecure Chinese-American teenager undergoes experimental surgery to appear white, hoping to secure the prom queen title and peer acceptance.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content: This is a solid teen body-horror, with a great way of conveying its message, lovely twists and engaging characters. The directing is outstanding, the casting on point and the effects understated and working really well. It might lack some of the shock of something like The Substance, but it is a worthy inclusion into your body-horror watchlist, certainly.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In an attempt to fit in and win prom queen, an insecure Chinese-American teenager undergoes a dark experimental surgery to transform into a white girl, only to face horrifying consequences as her true identity fights back.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Insecure Chinese-American teenager Joan Huang desperately longs for social acceptance and the coveted title of high school prom queen. Driven by feelings of inadequacy, she undergoes a radical experimental surgery at a shadowy clinic that physically transforms her into a white girl. While her new identity grants her instant popularity, it quickly detaches her from her heritage, family, and true self. Ultimately, as the surgical procedure begins to horrifically unravel, Joan must confront the true price of total assimilation.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Chinese-American high school student Joan Huang feels perpetually alienated by her white peers and dreams of becoming prom queen. Believing she can only gain acceptance by looking like past winners, she contacts Ethnos, a clinic offering an experimental plastic surgery that turns people of color white. Joan tricks her mother into signing a consent form and undergoes the radical procedure, re-emerging at school as a blonde white teenager named Jo Hunt. Presenting as white, Jo is instantly welcomed into the popular clique and secures the social influence she always craved. However, maintaining her status forces her to betray her original friends, distance herself from her parents, and erase her cultural roots. Horrifying side effects soon manifest as her synthetic skin begins to decompose and peel away, revealing her original skin tone underneath. On prom night, Jo wins the crown, but her face catastrophically deteriorates on stage in front of the entire school. Discovering the hollow lives of those who traded their heritage for conformity, Joan returns home to reconcile with her family. Rejecting the clinic's permanent pressure to assimilate, Joan violently sheds her artificial white exterior and tearfully learns to embrace her true self.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Joan Huang is an insecure Chinese-American high schooler who feels invisible among her peers and longs to win her school's coveted prom queen title. Convinced that she will never achieve acceptance or beauty in her own skin, Joan discovers Ethnos, a controversial scientific clinic that offers an experimental cosmetic procedure designed to transform people of color into white individuals. Desperate for validation, Joan undergoes the procedure and re-enters high school under a completely new identity, instantly receiving the privilege, attention, and popularity she always desired. However, as she navigates her newly elevated social standing, Joan is forced to confront the dark reality of her choice—including the painful erosion of her family bonds, the loss of her cultural heritage, and terrifying physical side effects. Blending body horror, dark comedy, sci-fi, and social commentary, Slanted is a sharp satire about the extreme lengths of assimilation and the true cost of erasing oneself to fit in.

story_structure.resolution: In the aftermath of the night, she reevaluates what acceptance really means and comes to terms with her authentic self.
story_structure.introduction: An insecure Chinese-American high schooler, desperate for peer validation and the prom queen crown, struggles with her cultural identity and feelings of alienation.
story_structure.risingAction: As she navigates her new appearance, she initially gains the popularity and attention she desired, but soon faces the unexpected social, emotional, and psychological fallout of erasing her heritage.
